description:
crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:138-159 implements `validate_id` with this rule:

    SAFE-CHAR = 0x21..=0x7E excluding 0x22 (DQUOTE)

So `Id::new_validated` accepts characters like `#` `!` `$` `%` `&` `'`
`(` `)` `*` `+` `,` `.` `/` `:` `;` `<` `=` `>` `?` `@` `[` `\\` `]` `^`
`` ` `` `{` `|` `}` `~`.

But RFC 8620 §1.2 (rfc8620.txt lines 287-296 in this repo) says:

    Where \"Id\" is given as a data type, it means a \"String\" of at least
    1 and a maximum of 255 octets in size, and it MUST only contain
    characters from the \"URL and Filename Safe\" base64 alphabet, as
    defined in Section 5 of [RFC4648], excluding the pad character (\"=\").
    This means the allowed characters are the ASCII alphanumeric
    characters (\"A-Za-z0-9\"), hyphen (\"-\"), and underscore (\"_\").

The rustdoc in id.rs:20-24 even correctly cites the spec:

    /// Character set: URL-safe base64 alphabet (A-Za-z0-9, `-`, `_`), max 255 octets.

So the rustdoc claims spec-correct validation; the implementation
delivers a much looser validator. The validator does NOT match its own
documentation.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. `Id::new_validated(\"#root\")` succeeds in this crate but `#root` would
   be rejected by a spec-compliant downstream JMAP server. Caller writes
   defensive code in their own validator that does `Id::new_validated`
   plus a re-check of the alphabet.
2. The `# Errors` contract of `new_validated` is ambiguous: callers
   cannot tell whether the validator enforces the RFC or some looser
   internal rule.
3. A future fix that tightens the validator to the spec is a *behavior
   change* visible to every caller. It would be a minor-bump
   bug-fix... but if any caller is currently in production passing
   non-base64 ids that happen to work today (e.g. URL-encoded
   characters), the fix breaks them.

Fix candidates:
- Tighten `validate_id` to match the rustdoc: reject any character
  outside `A-Za-z0-9-_`. Treat this as a 0.1.2 bug-fix (the validator's
  rustdoc claims spec compliance, so the looser behavior is a defect,
  not an API). Add a `# Errors` section listing the categories
  explicitly. Verify with a test that injects each of the now-rejected
  characters.
- Or: weaken the rustdoc to match the implementation, accepting that
  `new_validated` is not RFC-compliant and documenting the divergence.
  Less honest than option 1.

The SAFE-CHAR rule in the current validator looks lifted from a
different spec (possibly RFC 5424 PRINTUSASCII or RFC 5322 atext-like).
Whatever the source, it is not RFC 8620's alphabet.
title: Id::new_validated accepts wider character set than RFC 8620 1.2 and than its own rustdoc claims
